name: Floodlight plan mark
summary: Plan mark for a floodlight that lights an area, drawn as a luminaire with a widening beam.
description: Floodlights for yards, sports areas, facades and car parks are drawn as a luminaire mark with diverging beam lines, showing a wide spread. The aiming direction is shown by the beam and mounting height is noted.

Floodlights are typically controlled by a photocell, time switch or contactor because the load is large. The plan symbol often sits on a building wall or a pole and is linked to that control scheme. Beam lines are indicative. Photometric calculations, not the symbol, confirm coverage.
readingNotes: Note aiming direction and mounting height.
distinction: A spotlight has a single narrow beam arrow; a floodlight shows a diverging beam.
